To establish these results we develop perturbation techniques to create blender horseshoes in the real-analytic setting and import ideas from control theory which show that, typically, these objects have a large domain of influence.
item.dc:creator: Jaime Paradela

item.title: Stable Initial-State Recovery from Dynamical Samples using Nagy-Type and Pollard-Hilding-Type Frame Perturbations
item.description: arXiv:2606.08066v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Stimulated by Aldroubi and his collaborator's recent work on dynamical sampling, we consider a homogeneous discrete dynamical system of the form $f_n = A f_{n-1}= A^{n}f, \quad f_0 = f$, where A is a bounded linear operator on a separable Hilbert space H, which is known as the evolution operator, and $f_0 \in \mathcal{H}$ is the unknown initial state. The associated dynamical samples are given by the collection $\{\langle A^n f, g\rangle: g \in \mathcal{G, 0 \leq n < n < L(g)}\}$, where $\mathcal{G} \subset H$, is a finite or countable sampling set and $L$ is a function $L: G \rightarrow \mathbb{N} \bigcup \{\infty\}$. We analyze the stability of perturbed dynamical sampling systems in the sense of Nagy and Pollard-Hilding. More precisely, we establish sufficient conditions for the stable recovery of an initial state from perturbed dynamical samples obtained by changing the sampling vector, the evolution operator, ro simultaneously both, within the framework of Nagy-type and Pollard-Hilding-type perturbation of frames.
item.dc:creator: Ruchi, Lalit Kumar Vashisht

item.title: Partial Observation of Linear Systems with the Mori-Zwanzig Formalism
item.description: arXiv:2606.23341v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Mori-Zwanzig formalism provides a systematic framework for deriving reduced-order model of dynamical systems when only part of the state is observed, but its practical use is often limited by the complexity of the resulting computations. This paper develops an explicit formulation of the Mori-Zwanzig equation for linear time-invariant systems under partially observed observables. By expressing the dynamics in terms of observables, the Koopman generator, and projections onto resolved and unresolved components, we derive closed-form representations of the Markovian, noise, and memory contributions that arise in the Mori-Zwanzig identity. For the linear setting, the resulting formulas recover the reduced dynamics obtained from the variation-of-constants formula while retaining the operator-based structure of the Mori-Zwanzig approach. This makes the derivation a transparent reference case for reduced-order modelling with memory and clarifies how unresolved variables influence the observed dynamics through history-dependent terms. The analysis also identifies the ingredients needed for extensions to nonlinear systems and more general projections, including spectral filtering and data-driven approximations of memory effects. Analytical and numerical examples involving the harmonic oscillator and wave equations illustrate the construction and demonstrate how the formalism can be used to obtain interpretable reduced-order models for partially observed systems.
item.dc:creator: Fan Wang, Peter Benner, Jan Heiland

item.title: Lumping of reaction networks: Generic and critical parameters
item.description: arXiv:2606.28895v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate linear lumping for parameter-dependent mass action reaction networks, distinguishing between generic and critical parameter regimes. For generic parameters -- those ranging in some non-empty open subset of parameter space -- we prove that exact linear lumping yields only "obvious" reductions: elimination of non-reactant species or projections along stoichiometric first integrals. This characterization extends to reaction networks with product-form kinetics, including Michaelis-Menten and Hill-type rate laws. For mass action systems we proceed to develop an algorithmic approach to identify critical parameter sets -- algebraic subvarieties in parameter space where non-trivial lumpings become available. This procedure reduces the determination of lumping maps to a system of finitely many polynomial equations. It also applies to constrained lumping scenarios (which are frequently motivated by chemical considerations). We then review and extend results about proper lumpings. Finally, we discuss lumpings of a self-replicator system, and of a two-pathway enzyme mechanism, to document the viability of our methods in relevant scenarios. Our results clarify the relationship between structural (parameter-independent) and fine-tuned (parameter-dependent) reductions, with implications for approximate lumping when system parameters lie near critical values
item.dc:creator: Justin Eilertsen, Valery G. Romanovski, Santiago Schnell, Sebastian Walcher

item.title: Qualitative Analysis of a Two-Compartment Pharmacokinetic Model for Human Ethanol Metabolism and Its Generalization
item.description: arXiv:2608.09151v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work, we revisit a continuous-time two-compartment pharmacokinetic model of human ethanol metabolism originally proposed by Levitt and Levitt. We first establish the positivity of the solutions, investigate the existence and uniqueness of a positive equilibrium, and analyze its local and global asymptotic stability. As a result, the global dynamics of the original ethanol metabolism model is characterized, thereby complementing and extending the analytical results reported in the original study. Second, building upon the foundational two-compartment model of Levitt and Levitt, we replace the Michaelis--Menten metabolism rate with a general class of nonlinear functions, including both monotone and nonmonotone forms. This generalization allows us to examine a wider range of physiologically motivated scenarios and reveals richer dynamical behavior. We then establish the positivity of the solutions, study the existence and asymptotic stability of equilibria, and analyze the long-term dynamics under different ethanol input conditions. In particular, for a specific nonmonotone family, we establish the occurrence of a nondegenerate saddle-node bifurcation through center-manifold analysis. Furthermore, we prove the absence of nonconstant periodic orbits in the generalized model without assuming monotonicity of the metabolic rate functions. These findings extend the qualitative analysis beyond equilibrium stability and provide further insights into the complex dynamics of human ethanol metabolism. Finally, numerical experiments are conducted to illustrate the theoretical findings. The numerical results provide further support for the theoretical analysis.
item.dc:creator: Manh Tuan Hoang

item.title: On the horizon problem over the product of self-similar fractals
item.description: arXiv:2608.21047v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we first investigate the box dimension results for the graphs of continuous functions defined on $\mathfrak{F\times F}$, where $\mathfrak{F}$ is the self-similar fractal generated by an iterated function system (IFS) exhibiting the open set condition (OSC). Following this, we manifest the existence of a prevalent surface, defined by a continuous function on $\mathfrak{F\times F}$, that satisfies the horizon property in relation to the box dimension, i.e., the box dimension of the prevalent surface is greater than that of its horizon up to a constant $\eta$, where $\eta$ is the box dimension of the self-similar fractal $\mathfrak{F}$. Finally, we provide an example consolidating that the OSC on the underlying IFS of $\mathfrak{F}$ cannot be dropped.
item.dc:creator: Gurubachan, S. Verma, V. V. M. S. Chandramouli

item.title: Permutative lifts of strictly ergodic subshifts
item.description: arXiv:2609.01140v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Permutative sliding block codes - in the sense of Hedlund - give rise to finite-to- one extensions of subshifts. We provide criteria under which minimality and unique ergodicity are preserved by this 'lifting procedure'. These findings are illustrated by means of some nat- ural example families, which we use to obtain strictly ergodic finite-to-one extensions of sub- stitution subshifts (including the case of Fibonacci, Tribonacci, silver mean and noble means substitutions). We further study the interplay between permutative sliding block codes and Toeplitz flows. In particular, we find examples which demonstrate that a permutative lift of a strictly ergodic subshift may be minimal, but not uniquely ergodic - a phenomenon which cannot occur for primitive substitution subshifts.
item.dc:creator: Zeyu Kang, Tobias J\"ager

item.title: Thermodynamic formalism and multifractal analysis of Birkhoff averages for parabolic rational maps
item.description: arXiv:2609.20036v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study the multifractal analysis of Birkhoff averages for parabolic rational maps. We establish a conditional variational principle and prove the real analyticity and strict monotonicity of the Birkhoff spectrum, as well as the existence and uniqueness of the measure attaining the supremum in the conditional variational principle, on a certain region. To this end, we prove the existence and uniqueness of an expanding equilibrium measure and the real analyticity of the pressure function on a suitable domain. For parabolic systems, our approach using thermodynamic formalism provides a unified framework for establishing the conditional variational principle and investigating finer properties of the Birkhoff spectrum, including its real analyticity, strict monotonicity, and the existence and uniqueness of a measure attaining the supremum on a certain region.
item.dc:creator: Yuya Arima

item.title: Abelian maximal pattern complexity and extremal words
item.description: arXiv:2609.28059v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the Abelian maximal pattern complexity $p_{\alpha }^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)$ of infinite words over finite alphabets. For recurrent aperiodic words using exactly $\ell\geq 2$ letters, we prove the sharp lower bound $p_{\alpha }^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)\geq k+\ell-1$ and give a structural characterization of those words attaining equality for every $k\geq 1$. Without assuming recurrence, we prove that an infinite word $\alpha $ is aperiodic if and only if $\binom{p_{\alpha }^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)}{2}\geq k$ for every positive integer $k$. For aperiodic words over $\ell\geq 2$ letters, each occurring infinitely often, we further prove that $p_{\alpha}^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)\geq m$ whenever $\binom{m}{2}\leq(\ell-1)(k-\ell+2)$, for all positive integers $m,k$. Together with a matching construction, this shows that the minimum Abelian maximal pattern complexity in this class is $\sqrt{2(\ell-1)k}+O_{\ell}(1)$. We call a word an Abelian pattern Sturmian word if, for every positive integer $k$, its Abelian maximal pattern complexity is the least positive integer $m$ satisfying $\binom{m}{2}\geq k$. We show that a word is Abelian pattern Sturmian if and only if, after relabeling its alphabet, it is the characteristic word of an infinite set $E\subset\mathbb{N}_0$ whose bipartite incidence graph is a forest. This graph has two disjoint copies of $\mathbb{N}_0$ as its vertex classes, with a left vertex $r$ adjacent to a right vertex $s$ exactly when $r+s\in E$.
item.dc:creator: Qingcheng Zeng, Yumei Xue, Cheng Zeng

item.title: An application of the parameterization method to evolution flows associated to nonautonomous systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.18078v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional complete Riemannian manifold of bounded geometry. We consider a time-dependent vector field $X : \mathbb{R} \times M \to TM$ with $X_t:=X(t,\cdot) \in \mathfrak{X}^r(M)$ for all $t \in \mathbb{R}$ that satisfies some further uniform continuity assumptions. We suppose that $X$ admits a globally defined integral curve $\gamma : \mathbb{R} \to M$. To any isolated subset $\Omega$ of the Sacker-Sell spectrum of $t \mapsto \nabla X_t(\gamma(t))$, Sacker-Sell theory associates a subbundle $\mathscr{N}^\Omega$ of $T_\gamma M$ invariant under $\nabla X_t$. Under additional nonresonance conditions on $\Omega$, we prove, by an application of the parameterization method (Cabr\'e et al., 2003), the existence of an invariant topological submanifold $\mathscr{W}^\Omega \subset \mathbb{R} \times M$ with $C^r$ fibers $W_t^\Omega:= \mathscr{W}^\Omega \cap \{t\} \times M$ that is unique in a sufficiently smooth subclass of invariant manifolds uniformly tangent to $\mathscr{N}^\Omega$ (made precise later). We moreover show regularity of $\mathscr{W}^\Omega$ with respect to parameters, and characterize the attraction towards $\mathscr{W}^\Omega$ via a foliation in the case $\Omega$ is the slowest part of the spectrum.
item.dc:creator: Gergely Buza

item.title: A five-species counterexample to the Hofbauer--Kon--Saito conjecture on qualitative permanence
item.description: arXiv:2610.38374v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Hofbauer, Kon and Saito showed that a Lotka-Volterra interaction matrix $A$ with negative diagonal can be qualitatively permanent only if (C1) every cycle of length $\ge 2$ of $A$ is nonpositive and (C2) every negative cycle contains exactly one negative entry. They conjectured that these conditions are also sufficient, and proved this for $n\le 3$. We give a $5\times 5$ integer matrix with seven nonzero off-diagonal entries that satisfies (C1) and (C2) but is not qualitatively permanent. For an explicit integer growth vector, in which one species is an obligate consumer as the definition allows, the system has an interior equilibrium, and an asymptotically stable heteroclinic cycle on the boundary of the orthant attracts an open set of interior orbits. Adding non-interacting species gives counterexamples for every $n\ge 5$. The interactions form a one-way feedback loop together with a predator of two prey. The verification is elementary except for one heteroclinic connection, which lies in a face that is not Volterra-Lyapunov stable. For it we prove a connection lemma based on invasion graphs, which reduces the question to a smaller, stable face. The failure is robust. It persists under small perturbations, including weak additional interactions, so every sign pattern that satisfies (C1) and (C2) and contains ours is a counterexample, and it occurs for an open cone of growth vectors. For $n\ge 6$ there are also counterexamples in which every species grows when alone. Finally, we announce that the conjecture holds for $n=4$ and that, for $n=5$, four minimal sign patterns characterise its failure.
item.dc:creator: Beldiman Miruna-Mihaela, Halanay Andrei-Dan

item.title: New classes of reversible cellular automata
item.description: arXiv:2411.00721v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Cellular automata find applications in cryptography, error correction, theoretical computer science, and the simulation of physical and biological processes. We say that a Boolean function is a proper lifting if its induced cellular automaton is reversible. This paper introduces new classes of proper liftings, constructed through compositions of landscape functions, and explores their cryptographic potential by computing indicators relevant to differential and linear cryptanalysis. We combine theoretical and computational methods to obtain a complete classification of proper liftings for diameters up to $6$. Several open problems and conjectures are posed along the way.
item.dc:creator: Jan Kristian Haugland, Tron Omland

item.title: Distributed Adaptive Estimation with ISS Guarantees for Sensor Networks with Partially Unknown Source Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2511.07646v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper studies distributed adaptive estimation over sensor networks with partially unknown source dynamics. We present parallel continuous-time and discrete-time designs in which each node runs a local adaptive observer and exchanges information over a directed graph. For both time scales, we establish stability of the network coupling operators, prove boundedness of all internal signals, and show convergence of each node's estimate to the source despite model uncertainty and disturbances. We further derive input-to-state stability (ISS) bounds that quantify robustness to bounded process noise. A key distinction is that the discrete-time design uses constant adaptive gains and per-step regressor normalization to handle sampling effects, whereas the continuous-time design does not. A unified Lyapunov framework links local observer dynamics with graph topology. Simulations on star, cyclic, and path networks corroborate the analysis, demonstrating accurate tracking, robustness, and scalability with the number of sensing nodes.
item.dc:creator: Moh Kamalul Wafi, Hamidreza Montazeri Hedesh, Milad Siami

item.title: Circular orders: topology and continuous actions
item.description: arXiv:2512.17314v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the topology of circularly ordered sets. While the algebraic notion is classical, the general topological theory has received comparatively little attention. In this work we provide a self-contained topological exposition and present several new directions and results. Our aim is to initiate a systematic study of generalized circularly ordered topological spaces and of continuous group actions on them. Provide a convex uniform structure description of circularly ordered compactifications. This yields a topological analysis of Novak's regular completion and its uniformity. Demonstrate that this uniform-structure approach yields several new results in the theory of $G$-compactifications for topological group actions on abstract ordered spaces. Reexamine functions of bounded variation on circularly ordered sets and prove generalizations of Helly's selection theorem (for circular and linear orders). These developments and the systematic analysis of circular order topologies are motivated by recent applications in topological dynamics, particularly in joint works with Eli Glasner.
item.dc:creator: Michael Megrelishvili

item.title: Wave number dynamics in the real and complex Ginzburg-Landau equations
item.description: arXiv:2604.12847v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the large-scale dynamics of the one-dimensional real and complex Ginzburg-Landau equations using a scalar equation for the local wave number derived by a Wentzel-Kramers-Brillouin (WKB) expansion. For the real equation, the reduction has a conserved gradient structure. With higher-order regularization, we obtain families of exact stationary solutions and show that all nonuniform steady states are linearly unstable. These include localized holes distinct from the classical Langer-Ambegaokar hole. In the Eckhaus-unstable regime, the reduced equation develops finite-time singularities associated with phase slips. We derive a universal self-similar description of this process, with parameter-independent scaling exponents in good agreement with direct numerical simulations. The similarity profile satisfies a nonlinear fourth-order boundary-value problem admitting multiple numerically identified solutions. For the complex equation with nearly real coefficients, an additional Burgers-type nonlinearity produces wave steepening and traveling shocks connecting plane waves of different wave numbers. We derive the shock profile exactly and show numerically that the full complex Ginzburg-Landau equation converges to this prediction in the appropriate asymptotic limit. Outside this regime, the wave number profile becomes nonmonotonic, as explained in terms of spatial dynamics. These shocks differ qualitatively from classical Nozaki-Bekki solutions. The reduced equation thus unifies stationary holes, self-similar collapse toward phase slips, and propagating shocks within a common description of pattern-forming systems.
item.dc:creator: Yijun Lin, Adrian van Kan, Edgar Knobloch

item.title: Cost of one-relator groups
item.description: arXiv:2606.23506v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For any infinite one-relator group $\Gamma=\langle S \mid w^m\rangle$, we prove that $\mathrm{cost}(\Gamma)=|S|-\frac{1}{m}$. For such groups, this gives $\beta^{(2)}_1(\Gamma)=\mathrm{cost}(\Gamma) - 1$, answering a special case of Gaboriau's question on the relationship between cost and first $\ell^2$-Betti number.
item.dc:creator: Antoine Poulin, Konrad Wr\'obel

item.title: L2-L2-gain bounds for quadratic output systems
item.description: arXiv:2607.00552v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We derive an explicit bound for the L2-L2-gain of linear time-invariant systems whose output is a quadratic function of the state and the input. Such systems appear naturally in many areas, for example for port-Hamiltonian systems, optimal-control, and stochastic problems. In case the output is purely quadratic in the state, the bound is determined by the supremum over $\omega\in\mathbb R$ of the L2-norms of the bivariate transfer function restricted to the anti-diagonals $\{(s,\, i\omega-s)\mid s\in i\mathbb R\}$ of the frequency domain $i\mathbb R\times i\mathbb R $. Further, we show how the bound can be computed by solving linear matrix equations. This result provides a practical tool for assessing and reducing quadratic-output models.
item.dc:creator: Birgit Hillebrecht

item.title: One Shot, Twenty-One Balls: A Computer-Assisted Proof of a Single-Stroke Total Clearance in an Idealized Model of Snooker
item.description: arXiv:2607.12995v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Snooker folklore holds that no single stroke can pocket all twenty-one object balls. We examine the claim in an explicit model: twenty-two equal disks on a rectangle with six pocket points, under constant rolling deceleration, frictionless collisions with normal restitution, and lossy specular cushions. We exhibit a configuration and a stroke, and prove in interval arithmetic that every stroke in an explicit box around it pockets all twenty-one object balls, so the set of successful strokes has positive measure. That set is a ribbon: every speed from 9.3213 to 12 m/s works, while the certified window of directions is 9.4813e-43 radians wide, a number explained by a first-order analysis of twenty near-grazing collisions. A second configuration, a near-frozen cluster, has a certified window 9.4e-4 radians wide, thirty-nine orders of magnitude wider; its certificate uses Taylor models of degree six. The strokes with a given list of events form a semialgebraic set, and the endpoints of the windows are algebraic numbers. For the regulation opening position we state the corresponding conjecture, and show that if it holds with a regular witness then a finite certified search establishes it.
item.dc:creator: Avner Kantor

item.title: Density of the multidimensional Lagrange spectrum
item.description: arXiv:2608.30735v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Lagrange spectrum is a classical object in number theory, defined as the set of values of $\liminf_{q\to\infty} q\, \mathrm{dist}(q\alpha,\mathbb{Z})$ where $\alpha$ runs through irrational numbers. It has a complicated structure, with the discrete part, Hall's ray, and a transitional part in between. One can similarly define Lagrange spectrum in the multidimensional set-up, and until now not much has been understood about it. In this paper we prove that, unlike in the one-dimensional case, the closure of the multidimensional Lagrange spectrum is equal to the interval between $0$ and its supremum. The proof relies on a correspondence between Diophantine approximation and dynamics on the space of unimodular lattices and proceeds by studying a dynamical counterpart of the Lagrange spectrum that we call dynamical Lagrange spectrum. The latter is shown to be equal to the interval between $0$ and its maximum by means of an argument utilizing the higher rank nature of the set-up. A passage from full dynamical spectrum to the density of the Diophantine spectrum is achieved by applying equidistribution of expanding translates of horospheres in the space of lattices.
item.dc:creator: Dmitry Kleinbock

item.title: Terminal Blocks of Primes in Pisot Numeration Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.10026v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove a prime number theorem for fixed terminal block words in a family of Pisot integer numeration systems defined by canonical block expansions. Suppose that the dominant root $\varphi$ is a Pisot number and that the characteristic polynomial $P_h$ is its minimal polynomial. Then every terminal block word of total digit-length $m$ occurs among the primes with asymptotic frequency $\varphi^{-m}$. The result recovers the known Zeckendorf and generalized Fibonacci cases and extends the terminal-prime problem to irreducible Pisot-unit systems without assuming that the recurrence coefficients are monotone, that the canonical expansions are greedy, or that the finiteness property (F) holds. Explicit non-$\beta$ families and Pisot units failing (F) illustrate this extension. The main structural ingredient is a canonical block language whose expansion of the companion substitution fixed word records the corresponding integer expansions in natural order. This connects terminal conditions with Rauzy cylinder windows and then with a linear orbit on a compact torus. The required multiplicity-one geometry follows from Barge's pure-discreteness theorem after reversal of the substitution words. The same toral model yields prime genericity for finite factors of the substitution fixed word, polynomial sampling laws, asymptotic independence from fixed congruence classes, fixed-shift correlation formulas, and M\"obius orthogonality. Combined with established prime theorems, it also gives a terminal refinement of Chebotarev and arithmetic progressions inside fixed terminal prime classes.

item.title: When do lazy and invertible cellular automata generate all cellular automata?
item.description: arXiv:2610.18480v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $G$ be a group and let $A$ be a set with at least two elements. A lazy cellular automaton over $A^G$ acts as the identity except at the cells where a fixed pattern occurs, where it replaces the central symbol by a fixed different symbol. Let $M(G;A)$ be the submonoid of $\mathrm{CA}(G;A)$ generated by the lazy and the invertible cellular automata. We study when $M(G;A) = \mathrm{CA}(G;A)$. Since no lazy cellular automaton is surjective, every surjective element of $M(G;A)$ is invertible; hence $M(G;A) \neq \mathrm{CA}(G;A)$ whenever $A$ is infinite or $G$ has an element of infinite order. More unexpectedly, if $|A| = 2$ and $G$ has a quotient isomorphic to the Klein four-group $C_2 \times C_2$, then $M(G;A) \neq \mathrm{CA}(G;A)$. For locally finite groups, these are the only obstructions: we prove that $M(G;A) = \mathrm{CA}(G;A)$ if and only if $3 \leq |A| < \infty$, or $|A| = 2$ and $G$ has no quotient isomorphic to $C_2 \times C_2$.

item.title: Multiplicity of brake Reeb orbits on real prequantization bundles
item.description: arXiv:2610.29917v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove multiplicity results for geometrically distinct brake Reeb orbits on real prequantization $S^1$-bundles under geometric and dynamical assumptions. The lower bounds are expressed in terms of the sum of the mod-two Betti numbers of the real locus of the base. Our proofs combine Lagrangian Rabinowitz Floer homology with the index iteration theory for brake orbits. As an application, we obtain a sharp lower bound for the number of brake geodesics on Finsler spheres with pinched flag curvature.
item.dc:creator: Peng Liu, Dong Xie

item.title: One Polynomial Field for Every Euler Step and the Flow: Polynomial Dynamics for P and PSPACE
item.description: arXiv:2610.40025v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct, for each deterministic Turing machine that halts on all inputs, one polynomial vector field with rational coefficients that performs the same logical computation at unit Euler step, at every smaller or variable step in $(0,1]$ with divergent sum, and along the flow. This unifies discrete-time and continuous-time computation by polynomial dynamics, which earlier characterizations treated separately. For a machine making $T$ transitions in space $H$, a logical scale $h=2^{-s}$ with $s=O(H)$ suffices, with physical time $O(s(T+s))$, drift disturbances up to $h^{2K}$ for a fixed exponent $K$, and $2Ks+3$ fractional bits at unit step. On a fixed compact domain, polynomial time and robust eventual decision characterize P and PSPACE, respectively, with polynomial scale thresholds and no supplied stabilization horizon in the space case. Without sign, floor or conditional primitives, margin amplification at bounded speed, overlapping polynomial gates and interval-product estimates give the common realization, from which we derive shared logical traces, fixed-field PSPACE-complete prediction and a robust safety family with polynomial certificates common to all Euler steps and the flow.
